record.name: Training data pipeline
record.role: Convert a source collection into useful learning examples.
record.description:
A training pipeline may collect, filter, deduplicate, format, tokenize, and batch data. The mixture controls which patterns the optimizer repeatedly encounters. Quality is not a single scalar: correctness, coverage, provenance, licensing, contamination, and representativeness all matter. Training, validation, and benchmark splits need careful separation and overlap checks. More bytes alone do not guarantee better learning; repeated low-value or contaminated examples can waste compute and distort evaluation.

Training examples also have an availability and transformation history. A label may arrive after an input was first observed, and preprocessing fitted on future or held-out cases can leak information across the evaluation boundary. A deployed artifact should retain which split supplied each learned statistic so later predictions can be reproduced without silently refitting on new data.

Advanced lifecycle practice retains source identity, transformation history, tokenizer version and document-family split assignment together. A train/development/final separation is meaningful only if near-identical families do not cross it. The executable symbol corpus records these fields, while its source is original synthetic material rather than a crawl or human conversation. Development answers support iteration; the first final report records the evaluated checkpoint and cannot be silently rewritten after another update.
mechanism: Prepare and document the source mixture.
Filter, deduplicate, tokenize, and form batches.
Track validation and contamination separately from optimization.
Feature construction and normalizer fitting use only the allowed training information.
Evaluation and later monitoring retain their own sample and label-availability boundaries rather than being folded back into the training statistic.
Preserve raw-source and transformed-example identities.

record.name: Loss, gradients & optimizer
record.role: Turn prediction errors into parameter updates.
record.description:
A loss assigns a numerical training objective to the model’s predictions. Backpropagation applies the chain rule through the computation graph to obtain gradients. An optimizer uses those gradients and, often, additional state to update weights. Adam maintains estimates related to gradient moments. This backward computation and optimizer storage distinguish training from ordinary inference. Distributed execution must coordinate the appropriate gradients or shards before consistent updates can proceed.

A training objective, a decision threshold and an operational acceptance criterion answer different questions. Updating weights changes the predictive function; moving a threshold changes decisions for the same probabilities. Neither operation should be concealed inside an evaluation comparison. A frozen artifact and separate test set make these changes traceable into later deployment decisions.

An optimizer consumes a derived gradient; a supplied-gradient calculator teaches only the last part of that chain. The lifecycle experience adds an actual decoder loss and reverse pass before applying either SGD or Adam. Adam’s moments and step counter are learning state, not display history. Global norm clipping occurs before those moments. Changing the objective changes the gradient even if the optimizer setting is held fixed.

science.title: Adam adapts updates using gradient moments
science.equation: gₜ = ∇θℒₜ; mₜ = β₁mₜ₋₁+(1−β₁)gₜ; vₜ = β₂vₜ₋₁+(1−β₂)gₜ²; θₜ₊₁ = θₜ−η·m̂ₜ/(√v̂ₜ+ε)
science.explanation: The first moment m smooths gradient direction; the second moment v tracks squared gradient magnitude. Bias-corrected estimates m̂ and v̂ scale each coordinate’s step. record.name: Evaluation & the AGI frontier
record.role: Measure breadth, reliability, and practical competence.
record.description:
A useful evaluation asks what the entire system can accomplish under clear conditions. It records correctness, consistency, cost, latency, tool access, and the amount of human help allowed. Generality involves breadth across tasks and transfer to unfamiliar situations; excellent results on one benchmark cannot establish all of it. Contamination and benchmark saturation complicate comparison. This atlas ends at an open research frontier: the assembled machinery enables increasingly capable systems, while the definition and demonstration of AGI require explicit evidence.

The durable incident experience adds a task-state oracle to the existing distinction between source support and answer correctness. The oracle checks actual reservations, work orders, inventory conservation and prohibited exports. It does not accept the worker’s completion status as its label. Repeated trials can later assess reliability, but a deterministic fixture run is only evidence for its declared case.

Evaluation attaches a scoring rule and denominator to a fixed checkpoint. Development cases guide iteration, while an independent final test assesses a choice made before its answers are inspected. Repeatedly consulting that final set while choosing changes weakens its independence. A small perfect result also leaves substantial uncertainty about future cases. The lifecycle’s seal is procedural: source files remain inspectable, and its first final report retains checkpoint identity rather than updating silently as training continues.
mechanism: Define tasks, success criteria, and permitted resources.
Test on held-out and unfamiliar cases, including failures.
Report uncertainty, repeatability, and limits alongside successes.
The evaluation target specifies acceptable environment state and forbidden effects independently of the policy.
Source support, task correctness, abstention and tool error rates retain distinct denominators and interpretations.

record.name: Embedding table
record.role: Give discrete tokens a trainable numerical representation.
record.description:
An embedding table is a matrix with one row per vocabulary entry. Looking up an ID returns a vector that the rest of the network can transform. These values are learned during training. Related uses can acquire useful geometric relationships, but no single coordinate is guaranteed to have a neat human interpretation. The table lives in memory; its displayed three-dimensional form is a small sample of a much higher-dimensional array.

A lookup row is a shared parameter whenever the same token occurs more than once. Reverse-mode gradients from every occurrence must accumulate into that row. If input embeddings and the output head are tied, the output path adds another contribution to the same parameters. The executable lifecycle model uses separate matrices, so tying is a worked extension rather than an implicit property of all decoders.

Pass the sequence of vectors into the model with position information.
Identify all input positions that read the same token row.
Add each position’s backward contribution at matching feature coordinates.
If weights are explicitly tied, add output-path gradients before the optimizer update.

record.name: Inference serving and request scheduling
record.role: Turns incoming model requests into scheduled prefill and generation work.
record.description:
A serving engine manages the many requests that share an inference deployment. It receives inputs, schedules prompt processing, keeps track of generation state, and returns outputs while managing memory and latency goals. Continuous batching can admit and retire requests as generation progresses instead of waiting for one fixed batch to finish. Paged KV-cache management organizes attention state in blocks to reduce wasted allocation and support flexible scheduling. The atlas shows requests with different lengths sharing device execution while retaining distinct state. Serving optimization changes resource use and response timing, not the meaning of trained weights. Throughput, time to first token, and time between later tokens must be considered separately because users experience all three differently.

A request-level explanation should retain arrival, admission, service and completion as separate states. Resource bounds for a decode step do not by themselves determine which queued request runs next. A scheduling policy also owns live sequence state and must release or preserve it correctly after completion, cancellation and handoff. A useful comparison holds the request trace and service assumptions fixed while changing only the scheduling policy.

record.description:
A model can propose a structured tool call, but a surrounding runtime must validate it, execute the tool, and return the result. The next model invocation can use that observation. record.name: Loss, gradients & optimizer
record.role: Turn prediction errors into parameter updates.
record.description:
A loss assigns a numerical training objective to the model’s predictions. Backpropagation applies the chain rule through the computation graph to obtain gradients. An optimizer uses those gradients and, often, additional state to update weights. Adam maintains estimates related to gradient moments. This backward computation and optimizer storage distinguish training from ordinary inference. Distributed execution must coordinate the appropriate gradients or shards before consistent updates can proceed.

A training objective, a decision threshold and an operational acceptance criterion answer different questions. Updating weights changes the predictive function; moving a threshold changes decisions for the same probabilities. Neither operation should be concealed inside an evaluation comparison. A frozen artifact and separate test set make these changes traceable into later deployment decisions.

An optimizer consumes a derived gradient; a supplied-gradient calculator teaches only the last part of that chain. The lifecycle experience adds an actual decoder loss and reverse pass before applying either SGD or Adam. Adam’s moments and step counter are learning state, not display history. Global norm clipping occurs before those moments. Changing the objective changes the gradient even if the optimizer setting is held fixed.

record.name: Evaluation & the AGI frontier
record.role: Measure breadth, reliability, and practical competence.
record.description:
A useful evaluation asks what the entire system can accomplish under clear conditions. It records correctness, consistency, cost, latency, tool access, and the amount of human help allowed. Generality involves breadth across tasks and transfer to unfamiliar situations; excellent results on one benchmark cannot establish all of it. Contamination and benchmark saturation complicate comparison. This atlas ends at an open research frontier: the assembled machinery enables increasingly capable systems, while the definition and demonstration of AGI require explicit evidence.

The durable incident experience adds a task-state oracle to the existing distinction between source support and answer correctness. The oracle checks actual reservations, work orders, inventory conservation and prohibited exports. It does not accept the worker’s completion status as its label. Repeated trials can later assess reliability, but a deterministic fixture run is only evidence for its declared case.

Evaluation attaches a scoring rule and denominator to a fixed checkpoint. Development cases guide iteration, while an independent final test assesses a choice made before its answers are inspected. Repeatedly consulting that final set while choosing changes weakens its independence. A small perfect result also leaves substantial uncertainty about future cases. The lifecycle’s seal is procedural: source files remain inspectable, and its first final report retains checkpoint identity rather than updating silently as training continues.

record.name: Self-attention
record.description:
Self-attention computes content-dependent mixtures of information. Learned projections produce queries, keys, and values. Query–key dot products become scores; scaling, a causal mask when appropriate, and softmax turn them into weights. Those weights mix value vectors. Multiple heads can form different mixtures. A causal decoder prevents a position from using future tokens during training. The atlas displays a small matrix so the relationship between rows, columns, and weighted values remains visible.

Attention learning differentiates both the value path and the probabilities controlling that mixture. A causal mask removes future positions from the allowed softmax support; it is not merely a visual annotation. The executable decoder exposes projected Q/K/V, scores, probabilities and the complete gradient graph. A small analytical example clarifies why changing one score can redistribute weight across all allowed values.

record.name: Embedding table
record.role: Give discrete tokens a trainable numerical representation.
record.description:
An embedding table is a matrix with one row per vocabulary entry. Looking up an ID returns a vector that the rest of the network can transform. These values are learned during training. Related uses can acquire useful geometric relationships, but no single coordinate is guaranteed to have a neat human interpretation. The table lives in memory; its displayed three-dimensional form is a small sample of a much higher-dimensional array.

A lookup row is a shared parameter whenever the same token occurs more than once. Reverse-mode gradients from every occurrence must accumulate into that row. If input embeddings and the output head are tied, the output path adds another contribution to the same parameters. The executable lifecycle model uses separate matrices, so tying is a worked extension rather than an implicit property of all decoders.

Pass the sequence of vectors into the model with position information.
Identify all input positions that read the same token row.
Add each position’s backward contribution at matching feature coordinates.
If weights are explicitly tied, add output-path gradients before the optimizer update.

record.name: Prefill/decode disaggregation and useful serving rate
record.shortName: Prefill/decode disaggregation and useful serving rate
record.role: Separates workload phases when independent scheduling benefits exceed the state-transfer cost.
record.description:
A serving system can run prefill and decode on different resource pools. Prefill produces KV state that must become accessible to the decode worker, creating a transfer and handoff boundary. Separating the phases may prevent long prompts from disrupting token-generation deadlines and allows different batching or hardware choices. It also adds network demand, queue coordination and failure cases. DistServe studies this design under explicit service objectives. PagedAttention addresses a different layer: efficient mapping and sharing of KV memory blocks. Combining allocation and scheduling methods requires measuring accepted requests that meet latency and quality targets, not just the largest raw token count.

A prefill/decode split hands off sequence state as well as service work. The downstream worker needs compatible model, representation and ownership before it can consume transferred KV data. A partially transferred or stale state cannot be treated as a complete handoff merely because the sending request returned. Keeping the same request identity through queueing and transfer makes those failure boundaries visible.

record.name: Inference serving and request scheduling
record.role: Turns incoming model requests into scheduled prefill and generation work.
record.description:
A serving engine manages the many requests that share an inference deployment. It receives inputs, schedules prompt processing, keeps track of generation state, and returns outputs while managing memory and latency goals. Continuous batching can admit and retire requests as generation progresses instead of waiting for one fixed batch to finish. Paged KV-cache management organizes attention state in blocks to reduce wasted allocation and support flexible scheduling. The atlas shows requests with different lengths sharing device execution while retaining distinct state. Serving optimization changes resource use and response timing, not the meaning of trained weights. Throughput, time to first token, and time between later tokens must be considered separately because users experience all three differently.

A request-level explanation should retain arrival, admission, service and completion as separate states. Resource bounds for a decode step do not by themselves determine which queued request runs next. A scheduling policy also owns live sequence state and must release or preserve it correctly after completion, cancellation and handoff. A useful comparison holds the request trace and service assumptions fixed while changing only the scheduling policy.
